[[File:FlightSimulator-SW2.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Luke Skywalker and Wedge Antilles exit an X-wing flight simulator]]
{{Quote|A device that simulates what you see and feel when you're in a fighter's cockpit. It uses computers, holograms, and inertial compensators to mimic almost exactly the experience of flying, so you can get in a lot of training without risking valuable machinery or even more valuable pilots.|[[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]]|<ref name="X-Wing: Starfighters of Adumar">''[[X-Wing: Starfighters of Adumar]]''</ref>}}
A '''flight simulator''', also called a '''holosimulator''', was a machine used by [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] to simulate take-offs, landings, and flying in [[Starfighter combat/Legends|combat]].

Holosimulators could also be smaller devices that allowed individuals to recreate or design combat scenarios. [[Plescinia Entertainments/Legends|Plescinia Entertainments]] manufactured the [[CS-Mark 10]] which came preloaded with its "[[Great Battles of the Empire]]" series.<ref name="GFT">''[[Galladinium's Fantastic Technology]]''</ref>

==History==
Holosimulators were used for a variety of uses, one being a part of training [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] pilots for job roles and for combat. The [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire]], [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]], and the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] all used holosimulators to train their pilots and prepare for missions. They were also used for entertainment.

[[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] was assigned a simulator run in the lead-up to the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. His demonstrated skill led him to be accepted to [[Red Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Red Squadron]].

One model of holosimulator was located in [[Jagged Fel]]'s room while he was [[Head of State/Legends|Head of State]]. It was a ball about two [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in height and able to replicate any [[TIE series/Legends|TIE]] model, including the [[Nssis-class Clawcraft|Chiss clawcraft]]. It had a top [[hatch]], like TIE models. The opposition to fly against could accurately be chosen, as well as the skill level and distribution of pilots. Fel was about to begin a simulation when a kidnapping attempt was made on him.
